findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the closed disposition set every triaged comment unit lands in (e.g. RELOCATE-to-ticket / RELOCATE-to-ADR / MOVE-to-code / MOVE-to-schema / CORRECT-in-place / DELETE-obsolete / KEEP / DO_NOT_MOVE), define what constitutes a 'unit', and state which dispositions count as 'non-KEEP' so 'every non-KEEP unit correctly dispositioned' is mechanically checkable.
evidence: Superseded AC-2: 'a shard recovering fewer lines than estimated is not a failure provided every non-KEEP unit in scope was correctly dispositioned'
9ce8 AC: 'Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination; nothing is deleted without a destination that already exists'

The 4-value destination taxonomy is defined (plan para 1; discovery.md:95-100) but the disposition set (KEEP / relocate / delete / correct-in-place / do_not_move) and the granularity of a 'unit' are not; a do_not_move block is retained verbatim (so it reads as KEEP), while corrected-stale comments are neither cleanly KEEP nor non-KEEP

ABSENCE: no section of the plan or 9ce8 lists the disposition labels or maps each to 'counts toward recovered lines / stays / gets a do_not_move entry', so 'every non-KEEP unit dispositioned' is not mechanically checkable
findings.finding: The disposition vocabulary the acceptance criteria depend on ('non-KEEP unit') is never enumerated: the destination taxonomy (history/architecture/logic/contracts) is fully defined, but the per-unit DISPOSITION set an executor must verify completeness against -- KEEP vs relocate vs delete vs correct-in-place vs do_not_move -- and the definition of a 'unit' are left undefined, and KEEP vs do_not_move vs correct-stale overlap ambiguously.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (supersedes) AC-2 ('every non-KEEP unit in scope was correctly dispositioned'); mirrored in shard 9ce8 ('Every non-KEEP unit in scope is relocated or deleted per its destination')
scenarios: An implementer working a shard must decide whether a corrected-in-place stale comment or a do_not_move-listed invariant counts as 'KEEP' when self-certifying AC-2/9ce8; without an enumerated disposition set the completeness check is subjective and two shards may classify identically-shaped blocks differently
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short 'Disposition vocabulary' subsection defining a unit (a contiguous comment block) and the exhaustive disposition labels, mapping each to its destination and to whether it is KEEP or non-KEEP, and clarify that DO_NOT_MOVE and CORRECT-in-place are KEEP-class (retained, not counted as recovered lines) while the four RELOCATE/MOVE/DELETE classes are non-KEEP.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add to each of 4b94/4fc1/ab77/ad16/da4c an AC requiring the shard to measure (by diff line-count) and record on its ticket the actual comment lines recovered.
evidence: Parent superseded AC: 'Each shard MEASURES and RECORDS on its own ticket the actual comment lines it recovered (by diff line-count), and this parent records the net total across shards.'
9ce8 corrected AC: 'The ACTUAL recoverable line count is measured and recorded on this ticket, replacing the unreliable ~970 estimate.'

Roster AC blocks for 4b94, 4fc1, ab77, ad16, da4c contain only: relocate/delete per destination, do_not_move-before-edit, verified-stale correction, no-load-bearing-loss — none about measuring/recording line counts.
findings.finding: Parent AC2 (each shard MEASURES and RECORDS on its own ticket the actual comment lines it recovered) is covered by only one of six children. Only 9ce8's corrected AC ('The ACTUAL recoverable line count is measured and recorded on this ticket') delivers the measure-and-record outcome. The other five children (4b94, 4fc1, ab77, ad16, da4c) have no acceptance criterion requiring measurement or recording of recovered lines.
scenarios: Five shards land without recording their measured recovered-line counts; the parent cannot compute the net total it is required to record, and the completion verifier for AC2 has no per-shard artifact for those five.
findings.suggested_fix: Replicate 9ce8's 'measured and recorded on this ticket' AC into the other five children so the parent can aggregate the net total.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add to 4b94/4fc1/ab77/ad16 an AC requiring each proposed new ADR/amendment to exist and be committed before any comment citing it is collapsed.
evidence: Parent superseded AC: 'Every ADR enumerated in the shard tickets ... EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it is collapsed -- destination first, then the relocation. This AC is met per-shard against that shard's own enumerated ADR set.'
9ce8 corrected AC: 'Each new ADR and each amendment EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any comment that will cite it is collapsed or deleted -- destination first, then the relocation.'
4b94 body: 'NO ADR in the 83-file corpus mentions web search' — proposes an ADR but no destination-first AC.
ad16 body: 'Three new ADRs: the unversioned additive-only attestation manifest; the Burr tripwire ...; gate context is never elided' — no destination-first AC.
ab77 body: 'Three new ADRs proposed from review_bot/' — no destination-first AC.
4fc1 body: 'New ADR proposed: Explicit init over silent-implicit tracker creation' — no destination-first AC.
findings.finding: Parent AC3 (every enumerated ADR and amendment EXISTS AND IS COMMITTED before any citing comment is collapsed — destination-first) is covered by only one of six children. Four children propose NEW ADRs to serve as citation destinations — 4b94 (web-search capabilities ADR), 4fc1 ('Explicit init over silent-implicit tracker creation'), ab77 (three review_bot ADRs), ad16 (three ADRs incl. attestation manifest, Burr tripwire, gate-context) — yet none of those four carry an AC gating comment collapse on the ADR existing first. Only 9ce8's corrected AC states the destination-first ordering for its ADRs/amendments.
scenarios: A comment reading 'see ADR NNNN' is collapsed in 4b94/4fc1/ab77/ad16 before ADR NNNN is committed; the citation dangles and the relocated argument is lost, exactly the failure 9ce8's correction identifies.
findings.suggested_fix: Copy 9ce8's destination-first ADR AC into 4b94, 4fc1, ab77, and ad16 against each shard's own enumerated ADR set.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a history-handling AC to each shard: reduce ticket-citing history to the citation; file a ticket before removing history that cites none.
evidence: Parent superseded AC: 'History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a ticket filed first.'
No child AC block contains any mention of history reduction, citation, or filing a ticket for uncited history; all six carry only the four generic ACs.
findings.finding: Parent AC4 (history that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a ticket filed first) is uncovered — no child's acceptance criteria deliver it. Child bodies discuss it (ad16: '36 of 38 history blocks already cite a ticket ... two costly untracked follow-ups that must be filed first'; 4b94: '85 lines are free wins — history already citing b690...'; 9ce8: history reductions) but none of the six children's AC lists contain a history-to-citation-or-file-ticket criterion. Child AC (a) 'relocated or deleted per its destination' is a related/precursor outcome, not the same measurable outcome.
scenarios: A shard reduces a history block that cites no ticket by deleting it rather than filing a ticket first, permanently losing the history; the parent's file-ticket-first requirement has no per-shard AC to catch this.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the parent's AC4 wording as an explicit criterion on each of the six children.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add to every child an AC requiring full tests + make lint + make typecheck to pass unchanged, and require inline pragmas and test-introspected docstrings to be placed on that shard's do_not_move list.
evidence: Parent superseded AC: 'No behaviour change: the full test suite AND make lint / make typecheck pass unchanged across every shard. Inline pragma comments (# noqa, # type: ignore, # ruff:, # tickets-boundary-ok) and any docstring a test reads via introspection are load-bearing by definition and go on every shard's do_not_move list.'
9ce8 corrected AC: 'No behaviour change: the reconciler's tests pass unchanged' — no lint/typecheck, reconciler-scoped.
Five other children have no test/lint/typecheck AC at all.
No child AC mentions pragma comments or introspected docstrings.
findings.finding: Parent AC8 (no behaviour change: full test suite AND make lint/typecheck pass unchanged across every shard; and pragma comments plus introspected docstrings go on every shard's do_not_move list) is only partially and narrowly covered. Only 9ce8 has any test AC and it is scope-narrowed to 'the reconciler's tests pass unchanged' (tests only, not lint/typecheck). No child AC mentions make lint / make typecheck, and NO child AC lists inline pragma comments (# noqa, # type: ignore, # ruff:, # tickets-boundary-ok) or test-introspected docstrings as load-bearing / do_not_move members.
scenarios: A shard deletes a # type: ignore or a # ruff: directive as 'relocatable prose', breaking make typecheck/lint that no shard AC verifies.
A shard removes a docstring a test reads via introspection, failing the suite, with no AC pinning it to do_not_move.
findings.suggested_fix: Copy the parent's AC8 (including the pragma/introspected-docstring clause) onto all six children, broadening 9ce8's tests-only AC to include lint/typecheck.

findings.finding: The parent AC requiring each shard to MEASURE and RECORD the actual recovered comment-line count on its own ticket is delivered by only one sibling (9ce8). The other five shards' acceptance criteria do not include a measure-and-record obligation.
findings.suggested_fix: Append to 4b94, 4fc1, ad16, da4c, and ab77 the same measure-and-record AC 9ce8 carries, framed as an output not a target.

findings.finding: The parent AC requiring every enumerated new ADR / amendment to EXIST AND BE COMMITTED before any citing comment is collapsed ('destination first, then relocation') is delivered by only one sibling (9ce8). The other five shards each propose new ADRs but carry no ADR-ordering AC.
findings.suggested_fix: Copy 9ce8's 'destination first, then relocation' ADR-ordering AC into the other five shard tickets, scoped to each shard's own enumerated ADR set.

findings.finding: The parent AC 'No behaviour change: the full test suite passes unchanged across every shard' is covered by only one sibling. 9ce8 carries 'No behaviour change: the reconciler's tests pass unchanged'; the other five shards carry no test-passing / no-behaviour-change AC at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 9ce8's no-behaviour-change AC (scoped to each shard's touched subtree, or the full suite) to the other five shard tickets.

findings.finding: The parent AC 'History that already cites a ticket is reduced to the citation; history citing none has a ticket filed first' is covered by NO sibling's acceptance criteria. Two shards mention the behaviour in prose (4b94 'history already citing b690...'; ad16 'untracked follow-ups ... that must be filed first') but neither states it as an AC, and the other four shards are silent.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the parent's history AC verbatim to each shard ticket that relocates history blocks.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the destination-first AC to doc homes: for 4fc1/ab77/da4c, require the target doc (bash-migration.md / config.md rows / event-schema.md entries) to exist and be complete/current before the corresponding comment is collapsed.
evidence: 4fc1 body: 'docs/bash-migration.md is the existing home' — relocation target, no destination-first AC.
ab77 body: 'Recovering more than ~34 lines there requires writing those doc rows FIRST, or the trim destroys documentation rather than relocating it.'
da4c body: 'reducer/_version.py:39-66 duplicates the wire-format changelog that docs/event-schema.md also holds in a PARTIAL, STALE copy... Two homes, one drifting.'
Parent AC3 destination-first clause names only 'ADR enumerated in the shard tickets... and the amendments' — not doc files.
findings.finding: Destination-first / consumer-impact gap for DOC homes (analogous to the ADR gap but not covered by parent AC3, which enumerates only ADRs). 4fc1 relocates ~126 lines of stale bash-migration prose to docs/bash-migration.md; ab77 states docs/config.md rows must be WRITTEN FIRST before trimming _config_schema.py or 'the trim destroys documentation'; da4c notes docs/event-schema.md is a PARTIAL, STALE copy ('two homes, one drifting'). None of these three children carry an AC gating the comment collapse/relocation on the destination doc existing and being complete first.
scenarios: ab77 trims _config_schema.py comments for keys whose docs/config.md rows were never written, destroying the only documentation.
da4c collapses reducer/_version.py's changelog into docs/event-schema.md while that file is missing v4/v5, propagating a stale destination.
findings.suggested_fix: Generalise parent AC3 (and the relevant children) from 'ADR' to 'ADR or documentation destination' so doc relocations are gated destination-first too.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add '...; measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings stay verbatim' to the load-bearing AC of 4fc1, ab77, and da4c.
evidence: Parent superseded AC7: 'No load-bearing invariant is lost; measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings stay verbatim.'
4fc1/ab77/da4c AC: 'No load-bearing invariant is lost' (no verbatim clause).
4b94/9ce8/ad16 AC: '...; measured-fact and anti-refactor warnings stay verbatim.'
findings.finding: Parent AC7's verbatim clause ('measured external-API facts and anti-refactor warnings stay verbatim') is only partially covered: children 4fc1, ab77, and da4c state only 'No load-bearing invariant is lost' and omit the verbatim-preservation requirement, whereas 4b94/9ce8/ad16 include the '...measured-fact and anti-refactor warnings stay verbatim' clause. This is a scope-narrowing for three siblings whose bodies clearly contain verbatim-critical facts (ab77: _mcp_llm wire descriptions, _config_schema read-via markers; da4c: SNAPSHOT-restore migration guards; 4fc1: inverted --out/--in and DC 8.17.1 204 facts).
scenarios: A da4c or ab77 relocation paraphrases a measured external-API fact (e.g., an HTTP-behaviour note), technically 'not losing the invariant' but altering the verbatim wording the parent requires kept exact.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardise all six children's AC (d) to include the verbatim clause.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm signing.py falls in ab77's scope and add it explicitly (including its security-invariant do_not_move entries and ~5-8 line recovery) to that shard.
evidence: Parent body: 'comment triage cannot fix three files. _store/event_append.py (791)... reducer/_processors.py (777)... signing.py (798) recovers ~5-8. Their comments ARE the replay-compat and security invariants.'
da4c body explicitly owns event_append.py and _processors.py; no child body mentions signing.py.
ab77 scope names root-level src/rebar/*.py but its body enumerates only _mcp_models, _mcp_llm, _config_schema, bridge_fsck, review_bot.
findings.finding: Consumer/scope-gap: the parent enumerates signing.py (798 LOC) as one of the three files comment-triage 'cannot fix' (recovers ~5-8 lines), but no child owns or mentions it. ab77's scope ('root-level src/rebar/*.py plus attest/...') would nominally include src/rebar/signing.py, yet ab77's body never references signing.py or its ~5-8 line recovery, and no other child's scope covers it. The signing.py comment recovery is owned-by-none in the child bodies.
scenarios: signing.py's ~5-8 recoverable lines and its security-invariant do_not_move entries are neither dispositioned nor protected because no shard explicitly claims the file.
findings.suggested_fix: Name signing.py in ab77's body/do_not_move list, mirroring da4c's explicit handling of event_append.py and _processors.py.

findings.finding: The plan's only no-behaviour-change verification is 'the full test suite passes unchanged', but a large class of in-scope comments are lint/type-checker-load-bearing pragmas (`# noqa: F401` on side-effect/re-export imports, `# noqa: E402`, `# noqa: E501`, `# noqa: F841`, `# tickets-boundary-ok`) that tests cannot observe — relocating or collapsing them breaks `make lint`, not the suite, so the mechanism does not detect the task's most likely silent failure.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (supersedes) — 'No behaviour change: the full test suite passes unchanged across every shard.'
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the superseded AC list: 'No behaviour change: the full test suite AND `make lint`/type-check pass unchanged across every shard. Inline pragma comments (`# noqa`, `# type: ignore`, `# ruff:`, `# tickets-boundary-ok`) and any doc string a test reads via introspection are load-bearing by definition — they go on every shard's do_not_move list.'
